priority.when: First action - run prerequisite scripts and git commands
priority.why: Scripts provide structured context; git shows authoritative change history

priority.when: After scripts - load planning and implementation artifacts
priority.why: Need full context of requirements, plans, and implementation to validate

priority.when: When looking for specific patterns or issues across codebase
priority.why: Efficient way to find security issues, style violations, or patterns

priority.when: When understanding code structure and architecture
priority.why: Provides high-level view of classes, functions, and organization

priority.when: Only when creating findings.md or updating tasks.md after user approval
priority.why: Stakeholder mode has limited write access - only for documentation

priority.when: When user approves remediation that requires implementation
priority.why: Engineer mode needed for code fixes; Architect for design issues

tool.name: execute_command
tool.purpose: Run scripts and git commands for context and change analysis

best_practices.practice: Always run prerequisite script first to get feature directory
Use git status to identify all modified files
Use git diff to examine specific changes
Check for uncommitted changes with git status
Verify tests pass with appropriate test commands

command.name: Check git status
command.output: List of modified, added, deleted files

command.name: Check for merge conflicts
command.output: List of conflict markers if any

command.name: Run tests
command.syntax: npm test / pytest / go test / etc.

tool.example:
<execute_command> <command>scripts/bash/check-prerequisites.sh --json --require-tasks --include-tasks</command> </execute_command>
# Parse JSON output to get FEATURE_DIR and AVAILABLE_DOCS # Then use these paths to load artifacts

tool.name: read_file
tool.purpose: Load planning and implementation artifacts for validation

best_practices.practice: Load required artifacts first (tasks, plan, constitution, spec)
Load optional artifacts only if they exist
Use line ranges for large files to focus on relevant sections
Read up to 5 files at once for efficiency
Build semantic models from loaded content

files.file: plan.md - Understand architecture and tech stack
Modified source files identified by git

tool.name: search_files
tool.purpose: Find specific patterns, issues, or code across the codebase

best_practices.practice: Use for finding security vulnerabilities (hardcoded secrets, SQL injection)
Search for style violations or anti-patterns
Find TODO/FIXME comments that need attention
Locate specific error handling patterns
Use regex for flexible pattern matching

tool.name: list_code_definition_names
tool.purpose: Understand code structure and architectural organization

best_practices.practice: Use to get overview of classes and functions in modified files
Check for naming consistency across modules
Verify architectural patterns are followed
Identify missing or unexpected components

tool.example:
<list_code_definition_names> <path>src/api/</path> </list_code_definition_names>
# Analyze output for: # - Consistent naming conventions # - Expected architectural patterns # - Missing components from plan # - Unexpected additions

tool.name: write_to_file
tool.purpose: Create findings.md or update tasks.md after user approval

best_practices.practice: Only write findings.md if --create-findings-file flag present
Only update tasks.md if user explicitly approves option A
Use consistent format for findings documentation
Include all severity levels in findings.md
Add remediation tasks to tasks.md with clear descriptions

findings_structure.template:
# Code Review Findings
## Summary [Brief overview of validation results] - Total issues: [count] - Critical: [count] - High: [count] - Medium: [count] - Low: [count]
## Critical Issues
### [Issue Title] - **Location**: [file:line] - **Description**: [What is wrong] - **Impact**: [How this affects the system] - **Mitigation**: [Specific steps to fix]
## High Priority Issues [Same format]
## Medium Priority Issues [Same format]
## Low Priority Issues [Same format]
## Positive Findings - [Well-implemented features] - [Good practices observed]

tasks_update_format.template:
## Remediation Tasks
- [ ] [REMED-001] [CRITICAL] Fix security vulnerability in src/auth.py:45 - [ ] [REMED-002] [HIGH] Add error handling to src/api/users.py:120-135 - [ ] [REMED-003] [MEDIUM] Update documentation in README.md

tool.example:
<write_to_file> <path>findings.md</path> <content> # Code Review Findings
## Summary Comprehensive validation completed. Found 3 critical issues that must be resolved.
## Critical Issues
### Hardcoded API Key in Configuration - **Location**: src/config.py:12 - **Description**: API key is hardcoded in source code - **Impact**: Security vulnerability - credentials exposed in version control - **Mitigation**: Move API key to environment variable and update config to read from env
<!-- Made with Bob -->
<scenario> <condition>Architectural issues require design review</condition> <target_mode>bobkit-architect</target_mode> <reason>Fundamental design problems need architectural authority</reason> </scenario>
<scenario> <condition>Spec violations or requirement conflicts found</condition> <target_mode>bobkit-strategist</target_mode> <reason>Specification needs clarification or revision</reason> </scenario> </transition_scenarios>
<example><![CDATA[ <switch_mode> <mode_slug>bobkit-engineer</mode_slug> <reason>User approved fixing 5 critical and 3 high-priority issues. Updated tasks.md with remediation tasks.</reason> </switch_mode>

tool.name: ask_followup_question
tool.purpose: Get user decisions on remediation approach

best_practices.practice: Use for critical decision points (fix now vs document)
Provide clear options with explicit outcomes
Explain severity context before asking
Limit to 2-4 options maximum
Make options actionable and complete

template.name: critical_high_issues
template.question: Critical/high-priority issues detected that should be resolved before proceeding. Would you like me to:

suggestions.suggest: Update tasks.md and switch to Engineer mode to fix them
Document them in findings.md and proceed anyway (not recommended)

template.name: medium_low_issues
template.question: Medium/low-priority issues detected. Would you like me to:

suggestions.suggest: Update tasks.md and switch to Engineer mode to fix them
Document them in findings.md for later review
Proceed as is (issues noted but not blocking)

template.name: pr_creation
template.question: Code review complete with no blocking issues. Would you like to create a Pull Request?

suggestions.suggest: No, I'll create it manually later

tool.example: <ask_followup_question> <question>Critical/high-priority issues detected that should be resolved before proceeding. Would you like me to:</question> <follow_up> <suggest mode="bobkit-engineer">Update tasks.md and switch to Engineer mode to fix them</suggest> <suggest>Document them in findings.md and proceed anyway (not recommended)</suggest> </follow_up> </ask_followup_question>

tools.tool: execute_command - Run git status and git diff
read_file - Load required and optional artifacts
Present findings in structured format (no tool needed)
write_to_file - Create findings.md or update tasks.md

efficiency_tips.tip: Load multiple files at once (up to 5) with read_file for efficiency
Use search_files instead of reading every file when looking for patterns
Run git commands once and parse output rather than multiple calls
Build semantic models from artifacts to avoid re-reading
Use line ranges in read_file for large files to focus on relevant sections
Cache artifact content in thinking tags to avoid re-loading

anti_pattern.description: Reading files one at a time when multiple are needed
anti_pattern.why_bad: Wastes tokens and time with multiple tool calls
anti_pattern.correct_approach: Use read_file with multiple file elements (up to 5)

anti_pattern.description: Running git diff multiple times for different files
anti_pattern.correct_approach: Run git diff once and parse all changes
Always get explicit approval before writing files

anti_pattern.why_bad: Confuses user and breaks workflow continuity
anti_pattern.correct_approach: Provide specific reason explaining why mode switch is needed
